questions.question: Explain the difference between the Earth's orbit and its spin, and what each gives us.
questions.expected_answer: The Earth orbits, or moves around, the Sun in a path called an orbit, and one orbit takes about 365 days, which is one year; every four years a leap year has 366 days. The Earth also spins on its axis, an imaginary line from the North Pole to the South Pole, and one spin takes about 24 hours, which is one day. The spin gives day on the half facing the Sun and night on the half facing away.

questions.question: Explain how soil forms, describe the three soil types and give two ways to conserve soil.
questions.expected_answer: Weathering by heating and cooling, ice, roots, water and wind breaks rock into grains, which mix with humus from dead plants and animals to form topsoil over hundreds of years. Sandy soil has big grains and drains fast; clayey soil has tiny grains, is sticky and holds water; loamy soil is a mix with humus and is best for plants. Soil can be conserved by keeping it covered with plants, avoiding overgrazing, building stone walls, contour ploughing and using mulch.

questions.question: Describe how sedimentary rock forms and how fossils form in it, with one example each of a body fossil and a trace fossil.
questions.expected_answer: Rock breaks down into sediment, which is carried by wind and water and deposited in layers; the weight of the layers compacts them, and minerals harden them into rock over millions of years. A fossil forms when a plant or animal is buried quickly in sediment, its soft parts rot, and minerals slowly turn its hard parts to stone. A tooth or bone is a body fossil, and a footprint or nest is a trace fossil.
